Average of squared errors: (1/n) Σ (y_i - ŷ_i)²
Iterative update θ ← θ - α ∇L(θ) where α is learning rate
Uses the gradient of the loss over the whole training set each iteration
Updates parameters using the gradient from a single randomly chosen example
σ(z) = 1 ÷ (1 + e^{-z}) maps any real number to (0,1)
L = -[y log(p) + (1-y) log(1-p)] where p = σ(θ·x)
Linear function g(x)=θ·x + b used to decide class label
Systematic error due to wrong assumptions in the learning algorithm
Error caused by sensitivity to fluctuations in the training data
Least squares with L2 penalty λ Σ θ_j²
Least squares with L1 penalty λ Σ |θ_j|
λ controls the strength of the penalty term in regularized models
Technique that splits data into k folds to estimate out‑of‑sample performance
Table showing TP, FP, FN, TN counts for a classifier
Proportion of variance explained: 1 - (SS_res ÷ SS_tot)
Step size α in gradient‑descent updates
Model captures noise, performs poorly on new data
Model is too simple to capture underlying pattern

takeaways: Linear regression fits a line by minimizing squared error.
Gradient descent finds parameters by moving opposite to the loss gradient.
Logistic regression converts a linear score into class probabilities with a sigmoid.
Linear classifiers separate classes using a hyperplane defined by a discriminant function.
Bias‑variance trade‑off explains why both under‑ and over‑fitting hurt performance.
Ridge and lasso add penalties to shrink coefficients and improve generalisation.
Cross‑validation provides an unbiased estimate of test error for model selection.
bank_note: The syllabi stress clear definition of concepts, derivation of formulas, and justification of choices in long‑answer questions.

bank.q: Explain the ordinary least squares method for simple linear regression. Derive the closed‑form solution for the slope and intercept.
Given a dataset of house prices and areas, use batch gradient descent to estimate the parameters of a linear model. Show two iterations with a learning rate of 0.01.
outline: Calculate parameter values after iteration 1 and 2

bank.q: Implement stochastic gradient descent for logistic regression on a binary classification problem. Explain why SGD may converge faster than batch GD.
outline: Derive gradient for a single example

bank.q: Compare ridge and lasso regression. Discuss how each penalty affects coefficient estimates and model variance.
Define the bias‑variance decomposition of expected prediction error. Illustrate with a diagram showing the three components.
A student builds a polynomial regression model of degree 5 on a small dataset and obtains a training MSE of 2 but a validation MSE of 20. Identify the problem and suggest two remedies.
outline: Suggest reducing polynomial degree or using cross‑validation
Explain how each remedy reduces variance

bank.q: Design a 5‑fold cross‑validation experiment to compare three models: linear regression, ridge regression (λ=0.5), and lasso regression (λ=0.1). State how you would choose the best model.
outline: Explain training and validation steps for each model
Select model with lowest average MSE
Discuss trade‑off between error and sparsity

bank.q: Using a confusion matrix, compute accuracy, precision, recall, and F1‑score for a binary classifier that predicts 80 TP, 10 FP, 15 FN, and 95 TN.
Explain why a linear discriminant function can be extended to multiclass classification using one‑vs‑rest strategy. Discuss its computational cost.
outline: Show decision rule for multiple classes
Comment on training and prediction time

bank.q: State the formula for the sigmoid function and explain why its output lies between 0 and 1.
A telecom company wants to predict monthly data usage (GB) from subscriber age and plan price. Write the multiple linear regression model and list the assumptions required for OLS to be unbiased.
outline: List linearity, independence, homoscedasticity, no multicollinearity, normal errors

bank.q: Critically evaluate the use of R² as a performance metric for models with many predictors. Suggest an alternative and justify its use.
